key_insight: DER-Fault is a large synthetic dataset that simulates how faults appear in distribution grids with PV, EV charging, and V2G under many realistic operating conditions.
engineering_relevance: It gives researchers a structured benchmark for training and testing fault detection, classification, and localization methods in DER-integrated distribution systems.
method: Built in OpenDSS using the Iowa 240-bus distribution system.
Sampled 60 representative hourly load conditions from 8,760 profiles.
Generated 19,800 cases across six DER scenarios, normal operation, and ten short-circuit fault types with varying fault resistance.
evidence_signal: Validation shows the dataset covers diverse annual loading and DER conditions, with phase-specific fault responses and reduced voltage disturbance as fault resistance increases.
watch_item: Because the data are simulation-based, model performance may not fully transfer to real feeder measurements with unmodeled noise, device behavior, or topology changes.
paper_title: DER-Fault: A Simulation-Based Fault Dataset for DER-Integrated Distribution Systems Under Diverse Operating Conditions
